subject.title: fix: failed cloud dispatch leaks the session's managed worktree

question: Should an explicit Delete Session action be allowed to remove a session-owned managed worktree after the service snapshot even when it contains arbitrary ignored files that the snapshot intentionally omits?
rationale: The patch deliberately changes an existing preservation path into an irreversible cleanup path; the service contract and user-confirmed deletion support that direction, but only maintainers can set the durable product expectation for ignored user files.

options.title: Accept explicit-delete cleanup
options.body: Treat the Delete Session confirmation as authorization to snapshot supported content and remove the session-owned worktree, with after-fix live proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve ignored-file worktrees
options.body: Keep the prior preservation behavior for worktrees containing arbitrary ignored files and address leaked clean worktrees with a narrower cleanup rule.

recommendation.title: Accept explicit-delete cleanup
recommendation.body: Treat the Delete Session confirmation as authorization to snapshot supported content and remove the session-owned worktree, with after-fix live proof before merge.
